sources_quoted.locator: Ashe (Ranger's Focus notes) and Graves (basic-attack notes)
sources_quoted.quote: "A flurry can apply 5 stacks of Black Cleaver's Carve to a single target as it deals 5 instances of physical damage." ; "each of Graves' basic attacks can apply up to 4 stacks of the effect, increased to the maximum of 5 with a critical strike."

The engine has derive_ally_effects / support entries (support_effects.py, item_support_effects.py) ... the ledger already tracks support_shield_received / support heals from items — reuse the same event shape ... assert in a /api/calculate fight WITH AN ALLY in the roster (enemies + allies lists are supported) that the ally's ledger receives the heal/shield.

step_1_game_value_of_carve.note: 0.06 × 5 = 0.30. The old leaf's fraction 0.3 is therefore a game-legal number in isolation — it is the 5-stack cap, not an invented value. The defect is not the fraction.

step_2_a_percent_armor_reduction_has_no_.conclusion: A 30% armor *reduction* cannot be represented as a resistance-independent multiplicative damage factor. The recorded factor 1.2 is correct only for a target sitting at exactly 125 armor at that event, and only if no penetration term intervenes (S5 makes the composition order-sensitive: reduction → %pen → flat pen). Carrying a scalar `factor` alongside `type: armor_reduction_percent` is the shape of a *second, multiplicative* application of a shred that the engine already applies inside reduce_resistance — i.e. double counting.

step_3_engine_documented_bc_model_does_n.conclusion: Even under the branch where an ally-sourced Carve legitimately belongs in this ledger, the documented BC model prices the shred at the averaged ramp (0.24, or the exact Cesàro mean C − C(C−1)/(2h)), never at the 0.30 cap. The pair (0.30, 1.2) matches neither the averaged model nor a resistance-derived amplification at any plausible corpus armor.

step_4_attribution_of_the_source_to_a_su.field_semantics: `support_*` in this ledger family means ally-provided (S8: derive_ally_effects / support_effects.py / item_support_effects.py, sibling field support_shield_received). So support_resistance_reduction = resistance reduction contributed to the subject by ALLY participants.
step_4_attribution_of_the_source_to_a_su.roster_reading: Bloodsong is quest-locked to the support role (S3). Black Cleaver is a 3000 g FIGHTER-tagged legendary (S2) — not a support purchase. In a roster named for exactly these two items, Carve is the damage-dealing subject's own item and its shred belongs in the subject's own resistance path (reduce_resistance, S5), while the support's contribution is Bloodsong's *Expose Weakness*, which is an 8%/5% "increased damage from all sources" modifier — classified by the cached taxonomy as damage.modifier, "distinct from resistances" (S4), so it can never be a member of a resistance-reduction list.
step_4_attribution_of_the_source_to_a_su.conclusion: A record sourced "Black Cleaver — Carve" inside an ally-contribution ledger credits the subject's own item to the support, and its scalar factor 1.2 re-applies a shred already resolved in the subject's mitigation. Removing it is the game-correct ledger.

step_5_index_check.observation: The removed element sits at index [5] — the sixth member of the list — in a scenario whose entire named loadout is two items, only one of which (Black Cleaver) produces any resistance reduction at all. Carve is hard-capped at 5 stacks / 30% (S1, S7). Under either reading of the list (one record per Carve application, or one aggregate record per source) a sixth Carve-shaped entry at the cap is redundant: it is a stack the game cannot grant, or a second copy of a contribution already present.

verdict_reasoning.old_value_correct: Rejected. The only game rule that would justify a Black-Cleaver record in an ally-contribution ledger — armor *reduction* is a debuff on the target, so allies do benefit — requires an ALLY to hold a 3000 g fighter item next to the quest-locked support item (S2, S3). And even in that branch the recorded numbers fail: the engine's documented Carve model prices 0.8·max_stacks = 0.24, not the 0.30 cap (S6), and a percentage armor reduction admits no resistance-independent damage factor — 1.2 holds only at exactly 125 armor (step 2). No source in the evidence tree makes the entry mandatory.
verdict_reasoning.both_wrong: Considered and rejected as unprovable. It would require me to name the correct replacement value; the sources support removal, not a substitute number.
verdict_reasoning.new_value_correct: Accepted. The subject's own Black Cleaver shred is resolved inside its own resistance composition (S5); the support's actual contribution in this roster is a damage modifier "distinct from resistances" (S3, S4) and thus not a member of this list; and the scalar `factor` attached to a `armor_reduction_percent` record is the signature of a second multiplicative application of an already-applied shred. Absence is the game-correct value.

residual_uncertainty.statement: The evidence tree contains no scenario definition (roster composition lives outside data/), so I could not read which participant holds Black Cleaver. If the corpus roster in fact gives an ALLY the Black Cleaver, an ally-sourced shred record would legitimately belong in this list — but at the engine's documented averaged fraction (0.24) with a resistance-derived amplification, not (0.30, 1.2); in that branch the verdict would be `both_wrong`, and `old_value_correct` would still be excluded.
residual_uncertainty.confidence: medium-high on "the old value is not correct"; medium on "absent is the exact right answer rather than a corrected entry".
residual_uncertainty.how_to_settle: Confirm from the scenario definition whether Black Cleaver sits on the subject or on an ally participant.
